headline: Boom, bust and back-office collapse: AI wealth soars while services exporters crack

events: Spring capability jump: agentic models reliably complete multi-day software, accounting and claims-processing tasks; enterprise agent contracts triple
Hyperscaler capex passes $750bn; US grid operators declare data-centre load emergencies in Virginia, Texas and Ohio; gas turbine order books sold out to 2031
Electricity prices up 15-25% in several US states, nudging services inflation; Fed pauses cuts at 3.5%
Large insurers, banks and telecoms announce 10-20% back-office headcount cuts; Indian IT services firms report first revenue declines
US-China agree a limited tariff truce covering chips-for-rare-earths; trade tensions plateau
Inflation spike to ~4.7% G20 average on power prices, copper and wage pressure in skilled trades; Fed and ECB hike once each
AI equity correction of ~35% in Q2 as monetisation lags capex; two neocloud lenders fail, private-credit losses spread
US presidential campaign dominated by 'jobs for humans'; winner promises AI dividend and payroll-tax cut for human hires
Philippines BPO sector loses ~900k jobs in 18 months; peso slides, remittance-like services income collapses
Second capability jump in robotics-enabled logistics: autonomous warehouses and trucking corridors scale in US and China
Wildcard: interacting autonomous trading agents trigger a 40-minute US Treasury flash crash; 10-year yield gaps 70bp before circuit breakers; SEC imposes agent-registration rules
Global unemployment peaks near 6.9%; youth graduate unemployment above 20% in India, Egypt, South Africa and southern Europe
Sovereign debt crises: Philippines seeks IMF programme; Egypt and Kenya restructure as tourism and services income and aid fall; Pakistan defaults on Eurobonds
France faces a bond-market revolt over pension and unemployment-insurance costs; ECB TPI activated quietly, government falls
Productivity growth in the US hits 3.5%, highest since the 1960s; corporate profits at record share of GDP
US enacts a 'Compute Contribution' levy on large model inference revenue funding wage insurance and retraining accounts; EU follows with a digital-labour levy
China's AI-led manufacturing automation deepens deflationary export push; EU imposes targeted safeguard tariffs but avoids wider trade war
Major new conflict: Ethiopia-Eritrea war over Red Sea access, fuelled by unemployed youth and regional proxies
Solar-plus-storage and small modular reactor contracts surge as hyperscalers self-supply; renewables reach ~41% of global electricity
Mass protests in Manila, Lagos, Cairo and Paris; 'human-made' certification becomes a consumer movement
Third capability jump in scientific discovery agents: first AI-designed drugs clear phase III; materials breakthroughs in batteries
World growth at 4.1%, the fastest since 2010, but labour share of income in advanced economies falls to a post-war low
Unemployment eases to ~6.2% as care, construction, energy and trades absorb workers, though at lower wages for displaced clerical staff
Governments still run large deficits: AI tax revenues offset only part of transfer costs; US debt near 129% of GDP
Firms using AI in production reach ~63%; debate turns to ownership of models and public compute stakes

winners: Frontier AI labs and hyperscalers with own power generation
Electricians, grid engineers, nurses and other licensed in-person trades
Gulf states selling energy and hosting data centres
losers: Services-export economies (Philippines, India's BPO hubs, Egypt, Kenya)
Mid-career clerical, paralegal, customer-service and junior software workers
Young graduates in South Asia, North Africa and southern Europe
Highly indebted European welfare states facing higher transfer costs
bullets: The world economy grows faster than any time since the 2000s, yet roughly 215 million jobs have been displaced and the labour share of income has hit record lows.
Electricity, not chips, is the binding constraint: data centres take ~6% of global power and set the political price of energy in the US and Europe.
Four sovereign debt crises hit services-exporting and aid-dependent emerging economies whose comparative advantage in cheap cognitive labour evaporated.
Inflation spiked briefly in 2028 on power and commodities before AI-driven price deflation in services pulled it back toward 2.5%.
Public debt rose further as governments bolted on wage insurance and retraining, financed partly by new compute and inference levies.
Trust in institutions has eroded to ~31/100 amid a Treasury flash crash, visible elite AI windfalls and recurrent protests.
Trade fragmentation stayed roughly flat: rivalry shifted from tariffs to compute export controls and energy deals.
Renewables reached ~44% of electricity, but gas burn for data centres kept emissions from falling meaningfully.
wildcard: A March 2029 US Treasury flash crash caused by interacting autonomous trading agents, sending the 10-year yield up 70bp in 40 minutes.
image_description: In a Manila call-centre tower converted into a vertical farm, a former customer-service agent in a 'human-made' T-shirt tends lettuce under LED lights while a delivery robot hums past a protest banner reading 'Tax the Compute'.
